correctedCritiques.con-sincere-error-grief-hallucination: Strongest feature: The reply cleanly distinguishes known falsehood from sincere mistake, grants that costly commitment legitimately evidences sincerity, and proportionately presents grief-related hallucination as a possibility without claiming historical establishment. Principal limitation: The suggested psychological mechanism remains underdeveloped, offering no treatment of multiple experiences, group reports, bodily-resurrection interpretation, the empty tomb, or how grief phenomena could generate and stabilize the broader tradition. Live burden: O'Connor must construct a sincere-error account explaining the accepted data while defending which reports demand explanation and which may be later or unreliable. Locked score: The very strong band reflects responsiveness, precision, calibration, and representational charity, tempered by comparatively thin positive evidence and an incomplete account of the entire dataset.
correctedCritiques.pro-hallucination-scope-and-power-object: Strongest feature: The response grants hallucination as the strongest sincere-error proposal and evaluates it under two explanatory criteria, addressing bodily-resurrection belief and the public empty-tomb datum instead of dismissing the alternative by label. Principal limitation: Its categorical insufficiency exceeds the psychological and historical support provided, because hallucination phenomena receive no analysis while the empty tomb's independent establishment and inspectability remain contested premises. Live burden: Craig must substantiate psychological limitations, establish the empty tomb independently, and compare hallucination combined with source development or misinterpretation instead of testing a single-cause version. Locked score: The very strong band reflects coherent two-part analysis, central responsiveness, precise burden contact, and charity, while evidential compression and reliance on disputed data restrain the conclusion.
